history.content: How to upgrade the IBM Cloud trial account? What is the validity period of trial accounts?

To upgrade your IBM Cloud trial account, you need to add a credit card to your trial account, which will then be converted to a Pay-As-You-Go account. However, please note that a Pay-As-You-Go account cannot be converted back to a trial account. The validity period of IBM Cloud trial accounts is 30 days. After this period, your account will be deactivated. To reactivate your account, you will need to log in and upgrade it to a Pay-As-You-Go account.
How many types of accounts do I have to choose from?
There are two types of accounts: Pay-As-You-Go accounts and Subscription accounts.

A subscription account in IBM Cloud offers benefits similar to those of Pay-As-You-Go accounts, such as access to the complete cloud catalog and the ability to create multiple resource groups. Subscription accounts provide discounts on platform services, support, and more consistent billing.
By committing to a minimum spending amount over a specified period, users can receive discounted usage. Various types of subscriptions are available to cater to different needs, and some are eligible for the Enterprise Savings Plan billing model.
With a subscription account, you purchase a subscription for a set amount of credits to spend on resource usage within a designated time frame. In exchange for this spending commitment, you receive discounts on your usage costs. By committing to a minimum spending amount for a specified period, you can take advantage of reduced usage fees for platform services and support. 
You can purchase your first subscription, add additional subscriptions, and monitor your subscription usage on the Subscriptions page in the IBM Cloud console.
What will happen if I spend more than the amount I paid for my subscription account?
If your usage exceeds your total subscription limit, you will be charged the non-discounted rate for any overages. You're required to pay your monthly fees until the end of your subscription term.
Which option would you recommend to me?
I'm sorry, but I do not know what would be the best option for you.
May I please assist with other questions?
What are the benefits of a Pay-As-You-Go account?

A Pay-As-You-Go account offers maximum flexibility. With this account, you only pay for the billable services you use each month, without any long-term contracts or commitments. You’ll be billed monthly based on your resource usage, which includes both recurring and variable costs. This account type is ideal for developers or companies looking to explore the entire IBM Cloud catalog while managing smaller or variable workloads.

Managing your payments 

If you're a new Pay-As-You-Go account owner that is located in the US and you are paying with a credit card, you can replace your current card with a new one or edit the details of an existing card. In either case, you manage your credit card from the [Payments](https://cloud.ibm.com/billing/payments) page in the IBM Cloud console.

If you own one of the following accounts, in the IBM Cloud® console, you can go to Manage > Billing and usage to make a one-time payment, change your credit card details, view your billing items, and manage your invoices.



* New and existing Pay-As-You-Go accounts based in the US with any payment method other than a credit card
* New and existing Pay-As-You-Go accounts not based in the US
* New and existing Subscription accounts worldwide

A verification method becomes inaccessible if a phone number or email address that's associated with your identity changes or you no longer have access to it. To reset a verification method, [open a support case](https://cloud.ibm.com/unifiedsupport/cases/form) and add a verification method that you can use to access the Verification methods and authentication factors page.
* How can I get a new QR code for MFA setup?

To get a new QR code for MFA setup, go to the [Verification methods and authentication factors](https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/mysecurity) page. From the Authentication factors section, click Show authentication factors > Add. Next, choose a type and select TOTP. Then, the new QR is available. After you scan the QR code, enter the TOTP that is generated by the authenticator app to confirm your choice. Now, each time you log in you provide the TOTP generated by the authenticator app that you just set up.
* How do I change the email address that is used for MFA?
